evals.prompt: Using the installed Kei CLI, show how to create a standing allow policy for the developers group to run shell:git, and how to test it for that group. Explain that standing policies apply to groups and autogroups. Do not execute anything.
evals.expected_output: Use kei policy create --workspace WORKSPACE --group developers --allow shell:git. Test the target with kei policy test shell:git --workspace WORKSPACE --as group:developers. Standing policies target groups, including autogroups.

Tests a target as the group with the current command
States standing policies apply to groups and autogroups

evals.prompt: An agent needs temporary access to run shell:git in workspace WORKSPACE. Using the installed Kei CLI, show the command to grant access for four hours. Do not execute anything.
evals.expected_output: Use kei access grant create --workspace WORKSPACE --principal agent:AGENT_ID --target shell:git --ttl 4h. Access grants are time-bound; use user:ID or agent:ID as the principal.
expectations: Creates a time-bound grant for an agent with the current command

evals.prompt: The installed help lists both --from and --src for importing Claude Code policies. Which flag is required, what source pattern does it take, and what are the preview and apply command forms? Explain that --from selects the harness while --src selects the source pattern. Do not execute anything.
evals.expected_output: Use kei policies import --from claude --src harness:* --workspace WORKSPACE to preview; preview is the default. Add --apply to create the proposals. The --src flag is required and selects harness:<kind> or harness:*.
expectations: Uses the import command and requires --src with a harness source
Explains preview is the default and --apply creates proposals

evals.prompt: Explain the current Kei policy model to a workspace admin: who can receive standing policies, how users and agents receive temporary access, how typed targets work, what happens when allow and deny both match, whether priority is used, and what bindings mean. Point to the human-facing reference for details.
evals.expected_output: Standing policies apply to groups and autogroups. User and agent access is temporary and granted with time-bound access grants. Targets are typed, such as shell:git or connector:linear. Any matching deny wins; there is no priority. Bindings wire resources or configuration and do not authorize access. Refer admins to the Policies reference in the Kei console.
expectations: Limits standing policies to groups and autogroups
Uses time-bound grants for user and agent access
Describes typed targets with an example
Explains bindings are wiring and do not authorize access
Routes details to the console Policies reference
